whatItFakes: A full person nobody watches who hears a world candidate's speech takes the mean shift of their group of like hearers (place, lean, age band, how readily they yield), weighed by the members' mean closeness to the speaker, instead of their own; one who joins a group later takes its mean so far, and a grouped hearer does not weigh retelling it at home.
why: Owner, Nov 9: "not to track everything at every day"; the level-of-detail design (docs/speed/off-screen-campaigns-as-results.md, stage 1 step 1). Per-listener speech delivery was most of a campaign event's cost.
replacement: Dropped Nov 10, 2026 (too in depth, owner): the estimate stays as the game's answer. Was: Opening a grouped hearer builds their own detail (that they came, what they heard) from the group's result and the record ids (step 3), and a household retelling read by group.
resolvedBy: stand-in triage T9 (owner, Nov 10: too in depth)

whatItFakes: A day in results mode (time nobody watches) runs the dated work and, on the first of each month, each engine's own onResultsMonth step (finance, health, renewal, residents, place-prices, jobs, macro, grievance); no person acts, no module's daily work runs, nobody moves and nobody campaigns in a skipped year.
why: The fast clock, part 1 (pool item core-fast-clock-part-1-a-results-mode-for-skipped-time): one year day by day took 41.5 seconds in the smallest measured town; the base that the later parts add their monthly steps to.
replacement: Parts 2 and 3 of the fast clock are on main (births, deaths and illness; prices, pay and jobs). Part 4 (elections counted from the voters) and the parts after it give each remaining engine whose daily work a skipped year needs its own onResultsMonth step, each the engine's own code at a monthly pace.

whatItFakes: In results mode (time nobody watches) the work engine records no shift for a full worker, since attendance is each worker's own dated decision and payroll pays what attendance earned: a full worker at a business, an outlet or a public employer earns and is paid nothing in a skipped month, and a pay period earned before the skip that falls due during it is not paid. Counted workers are paid their wages by the residents engine's monthly catch-up, and the jobs, economy and place-prices engines open and run their dated work.
why: The fast clock, part 3 (pool item core-fast-clock-part-3-prices-pay-and-jobs-in-skipped-time): paying a full worker for a skipped shift would write an attendance record with no decision behind it. In the measured town the work engine's commitments were about one job in seven; a day-by-day year with the work engine's day switched off moved the town's prices by under half a point and its share out of work by under one point.
replacement: A skipped month's attendance as a result the attendance writer admits without a decision (each commitment's planned minutes, the way counted workers are paid their schedule), then the payroll dispatch for every due date the month passed.

whatItFakes: A race decided in skipped time (results mode) is counted from the voters' standing views and the candidates' records with no campaign's effect: no door, poll, ad, speech or press week moves a voter, and a filing's petition gathers no signatures on campaign turns.
why: The fast clock, part 4 (pool item core-fast-clock-part-4-elections-counted-from-the-voters-in-skipped-time): no campaign day is played in skipped time, and the campaign's group results (core-speed-world-campaign-days-as-group-results, parts 1 to 3) are not on main yet to apply once a month.
replacement: The campaign's group results applied once a month in results mode, as core-speed-world-campaign-days-as-group-results parts 1 to 3 build them.
